test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What will be the difference in population 3 years ago and 2 years ago of a town whose current population of 1,60,000 is increasing at a rate of 25% every year?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Rate of increase** = 25% = 1/4. Population ratio (Previous Year : Current Year) = 4 : 5.

**Population 3 years ago** = 1,60,000 × (4/5)³ = 1,60,000 × 64/125 = 81,920.

**Population 2 years ago** = 81,920 × (5/4) = 1,02,400.

**Difference** = 1,02,400 − 81,920 = 20,480.

**∴ The correct answer is 20,480.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c318a2d095f6cae8bf5b92292d7b72e8f6397f628caeb76b4fe61a42dce5c8e.png] 

**Given:** Current Population (P) = 1,60,000, Rate (R) = 25%, Time (n) = 3 years.

**Formula:** Pₐgₒ = P / (1 + R/100)ⁿ

⇒ Population 3 years ago = 1,60,000 / (1 + 25/100)³

⇒ 1,60,000 / (5/4)³ = 1,60,000 × (64/125) = 1280 × 64 = 81,920

⇒ Population 2 years ago = 1,60,000 / (1 + 25/100)²

⇒ 1,60,000 / (5/4)² = 1,60,000 × (16/25) = 6400 × 16 = 1,02,400

⇒ Required Difference = 1,02,400 − 81,920 = 20,480

**∴ The correct answer is 20,480.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Population Growth Formula

For constant growth, Future Population = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ, where P is the current value.

Successive Percentage Change

The net change for two years with rates R₁ and R₂ is (R₁ + R₂ + R₁R₂/100)%.

Depreciation Rule

If the value decreases, use the formula Value = P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.</p
